statements.status_notes: gzexe, when mktemp is not on the PATH, created its temporary file at a predictable path based on the process ID without exclusive creation, so a local attacker could pre-create that path as a symbolic link and make gzexe overwrite a file the victim can write. Upstream fixed it in https://cgit.git.savannah.gnu.org/cgit/gzip.git/commit/?id=4e6f8b24ab823146ab8776f0b7fe486ab34d4269, which makes gzexe (and zdiff) create the file with umask 77 and set -C, first released in gzip 1.15, whose NEWS says gzexe, zdiff and znew no longer have a race when creating a temporary file on platforms lacking mktemp; see https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-41991. Alpine has not fixed it in its 3.23 gzip 1.14 package. The DHI Alpine 3.23 gzip package applies the upstream change itself. Read /usr/bin/gzexe and /usr/bin/zdiff in every published build of it on x86_64 and aarch64 (1.14-r2, 1.14-r3, 1.14-r4, 1.14-r5): 1.14-r3 and 1.14-r5 carry the upstream change in both scripts; 1.14-r2 and 1.14-r4 do not. The range marks 1.14-r2 and 1.14-r4 as affected and 1.14-r3 and 1.14-r5 and later as fixed.

gzexe, when mktemp is not on the PATH, created its temporary file at a predictable path based on the process ID without exclusive creation, so a local attacker could pre-create that path as a symbolic link and make gzexe overwrite a file the victim can write. Upstream fixed it in https://cgit.git.savannah.gnu.org/cgit/gzip.git/commit/?id=4e6f8b24ab823146ab8776f0b7fe486ab34d4269, which makes gzexe (and zdiff) create the file with umask 77 and set -C, first released in gzip 1.15, whose NEWS says gzexe, zdiff and znew no longer have a race when creating a temporary file on platforms lacking mktemp; see https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-41991. Debian fixed it in gzip 1.13-1+deb13u1 (Debian bug #1141442), whose changelog lists CVE-2026-41991. The DHI Debian 13 gzip builds 1.13-1+deb13u1+dhi0 and 1.13-1+deb13u1+dhi1 are rebuilds of that version: both carry Debian's changelog entry, and on amd64 and arm64 their /usr/bin/gzexe and /usr/bin/zdiff contain the upstream change. The range ends at the first of them.
